about: Development: not commissioned by our standards. Each tumor read against the same person's own adjacent normal tissue, so no other person enters the comparison; the last globe is a control, two different people's normal colon, to show what a difference between people looks like. The change is fixed by the measurement (the globe's block rule) and its count never moves; the slider only fades the unchanged background. These pairs come from the colon and breast tissue tests, already scored, so these pictures cannot change their results. In breast the tumor lights far more than the two-person control; in colon two people's normal tissue already differs nearly as much, which is why the person's own normal is the reference that counts.
